channel.title: AmitForHealth
channel.description: Essays by Amit Kumar on respiratory care and the business of Indian pharma.

item.title: The man who beat his own hospital
item.description: In Dombivli, an elected corporator assaulted doctors for not having a bed his own corporation never provided. The CCTV also caught the reason nothing will change.

item.title: The poster will not save you
item.description: India bolts the law to the casualty wall and calls it protection. The resident walking past it at 3am needs a punished attacker and a guard at the door.

item.title: The wages of fear
item.description: Mobs that beat India's doctors imagine they are punishing the powerful. The people they actually sentence are the patients no one will dare to treat.

item.title: The Right to Inhalation
item.description: Why India's lung crisis demands a new patient right.

item.title: Gasping for relief
item.description: A queue of 1.2 lakh people for a live-fish “cure” exposes the chasm between India's world-class medicine and the patients it never reaches.

item.title: The united airway
item.description: What a 10-year-old's three lost years can teach two specialities that rarely speak.

item.title: Montelukast in India: friend, or the enemy we refuse to name?
item.description: A diagnosis-led note for clinicians, pharma leaders and policymakers.

item.title: The long wait to say “asthma”
item.description: India carries about a tenth of the world's asthma but more than two-fifths of its asthma deaths. The reckoning begins in childhood.

item.title: The inhaler nobody picks up
item.description: India has one of the world's highest asthma burdens. It also has one of the lowest rates of inhaled corticosteroid use. These two facts are not unrelated.

item.title: The breath India keeps losing
item.description: Twenty-six years inside the inhalation therapy market: why the deepest pockets keep failing, and the patient who pays for what we won't say.

item.title: Deep pockets, shallow breaths
item.description: Why most companies fail in India's inhalation therapy market.

item.title: The ethics of influence
item.description: Navigating pharma partnerships without compromising care. A note to young doctors, from someone who has spent a career on the other side of the clinic door.

item.title: The wrong best-seller
item.description: Why a SABA-plus-ipratropium combination breaking into India's top 20 pharmaceutical brands is a warning, not a milestone.

item.title: The sales model nobody changed
item.description: Everything around Indian pharma has been rebuilt by technology. The way it sells has barely moved in seventy-five years.

item.title: Nebuliser in every home
item.description: The quiet medicalisation of middle-class India.

item.title: Zoya deserves ice cream
item.description: Steroid phobia, and the cost of misunderstanding the script. Why India's most misunderstood medicine sits unused on the shelf.

item.title: Every breath matters
item.description: World Asthma Day 2026 asked for anti-inflammatory inhalers for everyone with asthma. For me, that has not been a theme. It has been sixteen years of work.

item.title: Expensive air
item.description: Eight in ten inhaler patients aren't getting the medicine their doctor prescribed. That is a failure of the system, not of the patient.
